judged_text: createEvent ignores both the per-destination externalId that EventManager now passes and the credentialId parameter, always resolving calendarId from only the FIRST destination calendar (`mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId`). For a collective booking with multiple Lark hosts, createAllCalendarEvents calls createEvent once per host's credential, but every call targets the first host's Lark calendar: each non-first host's token gets a permission error writing to another user's calendar, so only the first host ever receives the event, and the stored reference's externalCalendarId (the passed destination.externalId) points at a calendar where no event exists, breaking later updates/deletes with not-found errors.

adjudication.rationale: Verified in diff: EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now loops `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)` and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` (packages/core/EventManager.ts), but CalendarManager.createEvent never uses the `externalId` parameter to select a destination calendar; it always calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` and only returns `externalId` in the result (packages/core/CalendarManager.ts). LarkCalendarService.createEvent still resolves `calendarId` from only the first destination calendar (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`) and ignores the passed credentialId argument entirely (packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts). Therefore, when `event.destinationCalendar` contains multiple hosts’ calendars (handleNewBooking pushes team members’ destination calendars for COLLECTIVE), each per-host createEvent call will still target the first calendar, causing wrong-calendar writes and mismatched stored `externalCalendarId` (EventManager now records `externalCalendarId: result.externalId`).
